objectives.text: Define input size, output size, representation, successful/failed operation and best/worst/expected case boundaries for a reused C algorithm.
Derive and check an exact vector of comparisons, moves, probes or visited edges for original bounded inputs without rebuilding the prior implementation.
Distinguish abstract work, instruction/cycle observations and static control-flow complexity, naming the model and observable required for each claim.

subtopics.title: Asymptotic bounds and finite scaling evidence

objectives.text: Supply positive constants and a threshold proving an upper/lower/tight bound for an original exact cost function.
Derive a multi-parameter bound that includes the chosen input/output sizes and explain why a worst-case claim differs from an all-input bound.
Construct a counterexample to inferring Big-O from a finite measured slope or to interpreting an upper bound as a tight or universal speed ordering.
Trace an original sequence on a reused stack/table and distinguish the largest individual cost from a worst-case sequence bound.
Build a nonnegative-credit or potential certificate and check the telescoping total at every prefix, including the declared initial state.
Explain why the amortized guarantee is deterministic rather than a probabilistic average and identify which allocator/copy costs the model excludes.

subtopics.title: From work to instructions, cycles and bottlenecks

objectives.text: Count an executed instruction mix for a reused C/assembly kernel and relate it to a declared weighted-CPI/clock model without assuming one cycle per instruction.
Compute model cycles, dimensional time and a bounded speedup estimate, then compare with target measurements and explain a residual or working-set change.
Produce a multi-measure cost vector including code bytes or branch events and a static connected-function CFG metric without conflating its graph cycles with CPU cycles.
Derive simultaneous live, allocated-capacity, retained and scratch peaks from an original timestamped lifetime ledger and reject overlapping/double-counted ownership.
Interpret per-function static/dynamic/bounded stack records and distinguish a call-chain bound, sampled watermark, static sections and process/cgroup resident accounting.
Report space complexity and measured byte categories separately, with target ABI/build identity and unresolved recursion/interrupt/allocator boundaries.
Declare N,M,B and fixed-item units for a single-disk external-memory model and trace original sequential/random block references under a specified buffer policy.
Calculate transferred/read/written/useful bytes and an amplification ratio only when its useful-byte denominator is nonzero, retaining cache-layer boundaries.
Compare abstract block-transfer counts with observed syscall/device/bus evidence and explain a warm-cache or buffering discrepancy without equating those layers.
Construct a same-clock event ledger for blocking and asynchronous reused components, identifying submit/return/completion and borrowed-buffer release boundaries.
Compute end-to-end latency, throughput and scoped inclusive/exclusive serial attribution while accounting for overlapping phases rather than summing spans blindly.
Interpret elapsed/process/thread CPU observations including process CPU greater than elapsed time, rejecting wall-minus-CPU as a universal waiting measurement.
Trace short transfers, zero/EOF, interruption, nonblocking retry and delayed errors through a reused read/write adapter while counting actual accepted bytes.
Measure bounded buffered read/write and requested synchronization phases separately, declaring cold/warm state, file lifetime and the persistence boundary.
Reconcile component-return timing, file size and device-byte accounting, explaining why successful write, complete transfer and requested durability are distinct evidence.
Choose and verify an elapsed/CPU/counter clock contract including resolution, adjustment/suspend behavior, integer conversion, wrap and read overhead.
Extend a reused harness with paired repeated consumed-result trials, raw samples, a declared quantile convention, warmup/order controls and an overhead sensitivity check.
Report uncertainty, outliers and observed deadline/jitter/tail statistics without labeling sampled maxima or quantiles as WCET or a universal deadline guarantee.

subtopics.title: Linux PMU counting and sampling boundaries

objectives.text: Record target/kernel/perf/event identity and permitted user/kernel scope for a bounded per-process observation, preserving denied or unsupported outcomes.
Validate grouped raw values and enabled/running times, derive scaled estimates only with positive running time and explain representativeness and counter-ratio limits.
Compare instruction/branch/cache events or sampling attribution with the cost contract, identifying workload, multiplexing and measurement overhead limitations.

subtopics.title: cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting

objectives.text: Inspect a permitted cgroupv2 hierarchy/controller/delegation snapshot and distinguish observation files from configuration and inherited restrictions.
Interpret keyed CPU-time/throttle, current/peak memory, per-device byte/IO and pressure deltas with units and scope, retaining per-FD peak-reset and writeback-attribution limits.
Compare a bounded workload with unchanged observations or a prepared delegated quota experiment, explaining quota/pressure effects while preserving an explicit no-root unavailable-controller route.
Build matching uninstrumented and instrumented variants of a reused single-threaded component and verify -pg/coverage or entry/exit hook build/runtime boundaries.
Record bounded hook/arc/call or gprof samples and explain inline, recursion/exclusion, dropped-record and caller-dependent attribution limitations.
Compare measured overhead and code/stack effects against the baseline, separating counted execution, sampled self time, estimated children time and off-CPU waiting.
Check the selected core/device counter presence, access, enable, processor clock and debug/interrupt conditions before claiming a cycle observation.
Compute a bounded modular cycle delta and clock-unit conversion, reject ambiguous multi-wrap intervals and compare empty-bracket overhead with a reused kernel.
Produce silicon measurements or a clearly labeled captured/static certificate, documenting timer/GPIO alternatives and refusing emulator timing, energy or sampled-tail WCET claims.

subtopics.title: Choosing useful measures and making a performance decision

objectives.text: Select a justified vector of time, latency/throughput, space, work, traffic and code/control-flow measures for an original requirement and explain the omitted observables.
Resolve a case where a faster measured variant increases retained storage, traffic, static test complexity or jitter, using stated acceptance limits rather than a single score.
Submit a reproducible evidence and limitations ledger distinguishing proved model bounds, finite fixture checks, learner runtime observations and conditional energy/hardware evidence.
